meaningMnemonic: There's something made of leather with some dirt on the bottom of it. It's a boot !
In the water is a barb on the ground. It's coral . Coral may look pretty, but if you slip in the water and step on it, you're gonna get scratched up. That stuff is roooough.
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means interval .

Put a lid on the mouth of a child and what will you receive ? At best, a very unimpressed look from that poor child. If you want to receive nice things, putting lids on children’s mouths isn’t the way to go about it.

Your flowers become your servants. You plant them, you water them, you bring them up, then you cut them down and put them in your storehouse . They do what you want because they become YOUR servants, not the other way around. That's why you can tell them to sit in the storehouse where they wait until you come to eat them.
The products trees make? That's syrup . Delicious maple syrup, for example. Mmmm!
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means wide .

On a cliff , a fire burns to ashes . The ashes then blow off the cliff, and follow the wind wherever it may go. Hints See the light from the fire as the ashes fly off the cliff. The wind carries some of the ashes over to you. Feel the ashes as they strike your face and wipe the black ash with your hands.
readingMnemonic: The ashes inspire you to write a hai ku ( はい ). Using the ashes you write a haiku on a rock for everyone to enjoy. Hints Ashes on my face. Falling from the cliff of fire. Gives my life meaning. Or just come up with your own haiku. Whatever works for you.

meaningMnemonic: If you see icicle s hanging off of a samurai 's clothes , don't worry, those are just part of his winter attire . Samurai have to travel and fight in all sorts of conditions, so it only makes sense that they have attire for every season. Hints Picture a samurai in his winter attire. His helmet is white and fuzzy and he has decorative icicles hanging down off of his armor.
readingMnemonic: Attire like this is important because it reflects your soul ( そう ). The samurai is wearing clothing with icicles because that's how his heart feels too: frozen over because he has to fight in this horrible winter weather. Hints Picture the kind of attire you'd wear as a samurai to reflect your soul. Mine would be bright pink and covered in horses and bananas and daisies to show that I have a happy, kind soul and that I don't want to be killed by anyone else.

meaningMnemonic: If you want to give flowers to someone , give them to an author . Authors really love flowers, because they help them think of flowery language they can use to sound smart in their books. Hints Imagine a time when a book you were reading used flowery language and you couldn't understand. Imagine the annoyance with the author for being so overwrought and flowery.
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately, the author is allergic to touching flowers, so they hold them with a pair of cho psticks ( ちょ ). They hold them real close to their face with the chopsticks, so they can still use them to think of fancy, author-ly words. Hints Picture the author trying to use chopsticks to hold some little flowers. It looks like they're having a hard time, but people will do anything to be a great author, I suppose.

meaningMnemonic: There's a lid on your village , so you kick it over on its backside to see what's on its underside . Hints You've been curious about what's on the lid (and your village's) backside for years, and you finally can't take it anymore so you kick the lid as hard as you can!
readingMnemonic: It turns out your village's own backside is covered in ura nium ( うら ). Eureka! You're all gonna be rich! Hints Wait, isn't uranium bad for people? This explains why all of the villagers' backsides are covered in weird glowing, green lumps.

meaningMnemonic: You keep your moon weapon in your crotch . Where else would you keep it? Hints Your moon weapon is a moon that you keep in your crotch. We'll let you imagine how this one works...
readingMnemonic: Your crotch has a moon weapon, and it's served you well, so you hope that if you have a 子 ( こ ) one day, they'll have one too. Hints Your mother had a moon weapon, and her father before her. It's been in the family for generations, and you hope to pass it on to your 子 as well.

meaningMnemonic: Put a rice paddy together with other paddies and you'll see how much they differ . When you're driving or taking a train through the countryside it may seem like all of those rice paddies blurring together are all the same, but they can differ quite a bit! Hints Try to picture how each rice paddy differs from the next. Can you think of any differences in the ones you've seen?
readingMnemonic: To see how rice paddies differ , you need an ea gle's ( い ) eye view. It can be hard to see from the ground, so soar up into the sky like an eagle and look down at the rice paddies together. Hints Aha! As an eagle you can easily see that all of the rice paddies have differing colors, shapes, and (if you fly low) smells. They differ a lot!

meaningMnemonic: Social commentary aside, the white king is the king that wears all white. Traditionally, this is someone better than a king. The emperor ! Hints See the emperor, garbed all in white. There are other kings, but the emperor's white clothing shows his status above the rest.
readingMnemonic: Who is the emperor ? It is こう いち . こういち the emperor stands over his subjects. Hints How did こういち become emperor?! His first decree as emperor is that everybody must learn kanji now. Note: from now on, Emperor こういち will be a recurring character for the reading mnemonic of こう .

meaningMnemonic: To make your fingers wide you extend them. Hints Extend your fingers right now and see how wide you can make them.
readingMnemonic: As you extend your fingers a cock ( かく ) comes running by and runs straight into them. Bu-COCK! Hints You poked the cock right in the eye with your extended fingers. Maybe you shouldn't be doing that in public. Innocent cocks could get hurt.

meaningMnemonic: Use a flag to compare your flatulence . Hints How do you compare your flatulence? I recommend a flag. You can see which fart is strongest by seeing how much the flag flutters.
readingMnemonic: How do you read flatulence ? Heh ( へ )...heh..heh..heheheh. You can't NOT laugh at the word flatulence. Note that some dictionaries incorrectly list おなら as a reading for this kanji. While おなら also means "flatulence" (as in "fart"), you’ll only ever encounter this reading in hiragana, as the kanji can only be read as へ . Hints Picture yourself unable to stop snickering over the word "flatulence", like a little schoolchild. Heh… heh…

meaningMnemonic: A greenhouse is already really good when it comes to a plant's livelihood. But add the sun into that equation and you have something really great for the plants. Their livelihood will be awesome, now! Hints Just feel happy that your plants have such a nice livelihood now that the sun is out. They look so healthy and fresh!
readingMnemonic: From out of nowhere, Bo bo ( ぼ ) the notorious clown thief starts picking the plants, ending their livelihood . Bobo needs the flowers for his clown acts, so he uses the livelihood of the flowers to support his own livelihood. Hints Look at Bobo do what he needs to do to maintain his own livelihood. Hear the flowers screaming as they are plucked from their homes.

meaningMnemonic: Those that are in the middle of your heart are the ones you have the most loyalty towards. The middle of your heart is the most sacred, special place for people, so it makes sense that those you keep in the middle of your heart are those you are most loyal to. Hints Who do you feel the most loyalty towards? Imagine them in the middle of your heart. Feel them in your chest. Imagine them, literally inside the middle of your heart.
readingMnemonic: You pictured Chew bacca ( ちゅう ), didn’t you? No? Well you should have. Chewbacca deserves everyone’s loyalty . Chewbacca is super loyal to you, so he deserves your loyalty back. Hints Chewbacca is very loyal. Focus on your loyalty to Chewbacca. Picture him right in the middle of your heart and hear his Chewbacca yell. Also keep in mind that this kanji shares its reading with 中 which is also included in this kanji.

meaningMnemonic: There is a moon and a city inside your lung . Inside of your lung there is a city and above that city lies a moon. It’s a pretty sight, but also very strange. Moons and cities don’t usually reside inside lungs. Hints Imagine having a moon and a city inside your lung. Feel their presence as you breathe in and breathe out. Also, 月 often refers to internal organs as well, so remember that when you see this kanji.
readingMnemonic: Having a moon and city inside your lung inspires you to write a hai ku ( はい ). Perhaps the city and moon are just metaphorical. Either way, a haiku is the best way to go about things here. Hints The city and moon Inside my lung, forgotten. Where is the answer? Or just think of your own haiku. Be creative!

meaningMnemonic: To say what's in a samurai 's heart you start a magazine . You go around writing about and interviewing all the samurai so you can share what they say to everyone who wants to read! Hints Why hadn't anyone thought of making a samurai magazine before?!
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately, your magazine helps the shee p ( し ) samurai find other samurai... and kill them. None of the samurai want to share their feelings with your magazine anymore, oh no! Hints The sheep samurai is ruining your magazine! Maybe you should start a new magazine called, "All the places the sheep samurai will be, so stay away!" to make up for all the damage you've caused.

meaningMnemonic: What might a leader say to someone to make little drop s of sweat appear on their brow? "Go make money for me." When a leader entrusts someone with carrying out their latest money-making plan, that person's gonna feel a lot of pressure to succeed. Hints Imagine you're that someone: feel the drops of sweat rolling down your brow as your leader explains their money-making plan to you. It's a good plan — you just hope you can carry it out properly and bring back some money for your leader! (Note that the drop radical can be dropped sometimes — that is, it's fairly common for it to be omitted in handwriting or in certain fonts.)
readingMnemonic: So, what's your leader's grand plan to make money ? Having you mow ( もう ) lawns, of course. Few money-making schemes are more tried-and-true than the ol' "mow your neighbor's lawn for twenty bucks" approach. Grass grows back forever, so it's basically nature's cash cow — moooow, get it? Hints You do a great job and pretty soon you're mowing lawns all over town, raking in profits hand over fist. Before you know it, you've built a full-blown money-making mow -nopoly, and your leader couldn't be prouder. Guess you didn't need to be so nervous about succeeding after all, huh?

meaningMnemonic: If someone has their fingers in your syrup , it's just another way of saying they manipulate d you. Cause only slimy people manipulate other people, so their fingers are slimy and sticky because they're covered in your syrup from mucking up your life. This also has another meaning: chastity . Just imagine if someone wanted you to keep your chastity and they called s.e.x. when someone "puts their fingers in your syrup." That would be pretty effective, right? Cause it's like, super gross. Hints "Ah golly gee wiz, he sure got his fingers all up in my syrup again, dagnabbit." You know, this saying we say all the time when someone manipulates us into doing something.
readingMnemonic: If you want to manipulate someone else it's going to have a permanent effect on your sou l ( そう ). Being manipulative isn't cool. And your soul will suffer forever for it. Hints What happens to your soul, you ask? It gets covered in syrup. That's probably where the syrup fingers phrase came from in the first place.

meaningMnemonic: This bamboo absorbed the moon 's power , and you want that power in your body, so you surgically insert them into your body to replace your muscle s and tendon s. Hints Picture your new bamboo muscles glowing under your skin with the moon's power. You flex and feel the power coursing through you!
readingMnemonic: Your special muscle s and tendon s have become famous and the Kin g ( きん ) of England has requested that you appear in his court! It looks like he wants you to teach his barber surgeons how you got your new muscles. Hints Imagine standing before the King, explaining in detail how you cut yourself open and replaced your weak human meat with the special muscles you have now. He's staring intently at you, but more so at your shining body than your mouth as you talk.

meaningMnemonic: No one is more full of life than the little man you call your nephew . Hints Imagine your nephew as a rambunctious, lively little boy. He's always running around your brother or sister's house and livening the place up with his antics.
readingMnemonic: Your nephew is so lively that you need to yell " Oi ( おい )!" at him sometimes when he comes to visit. "Oi! Nephew! Stop licking the window! Oi! Quit flushing my socks down the toilet!" Hints Imagine your nephew doing the most rascally, annoying little-kid thing you can imagine. Now let out your annoyance with a loud "OIIIIIIIII!!!!!!!"

meaningMnemonic: The Not Mouth says “ no ”. What else would you expect from something named the “Not Mouth”? The Not Mouth will always say “no”, regardless of the question. Hints Imagine encountering this Not Mouth. Ask it a question. It answers, “No”. Imagine doing this over and over until you believe that the Not Mouth always says “no”.
readingMnemonic: You ask the Not Mouth if it is afraid of he at ( ひ ). The Not Mouth says, “ no ”. So you set the Not Mouth on fire. The Not Mouth then screams, “NONONONONONONONONONOOOOOO~!” Looks like someone can’t handle the heat. Hints Listen as the Not Mouth continues to scream in bloodcurdling agony. Hear the flames flicker as they lick across the Not Mouth’s being. Seems as though the heat was too much for the Not Mouth.

meaningMnemonic: If you become a plate , I will pile food up upon you. With such a huge pile, everyone will think you're prosperous . Hints If you have piles of something, you're prosperous. If you become a plate, that's the best thing that can happen to you.
readingMnemonic: You're so prosperous you use your sa ber ( せい ) to cut the food pile and shove the bits into your plate mouth. In fact, your entire family is using your special saber to cut and eat off of you. A normal knife wouldn't be able to get through all this food! Hints You know a family is seriously prosperous when they don't use forks, they use a magical saber to cut their food. Wowee wow wow.

meaningMnemonic: Someone climbs onto the roof from the ground when dawn comes to proclaim that a new day has begun! They proclaim this at the top of their lungs! Hints Picture a shadowy shape on top of the roof, proclaiming to the entire town that the new day is here! It's come! And it's also time to get up.
readingMnemonic: The thing that climbs up on the roof to proclaim that the new day is here is a cen taur ( せん ). Ohoho, did you think I was going to say it was a rooster? Wrong! Centaurs are taller than humans and roosters, so when they climb onto the roof with their horse legs they can see dawn starting before anyone else. Hints Picture that shadow on the roof, proclaiming it's a new day, but this time make sure you picture the outline of this centaur. He has a human top half and a horse bottom half. And he's yelling down at you, "HEY THE SUN IS UP IT'S DAWN GET OUT OF BED!"

meaningMnemonic: The leader who is king of every shellfish sets the rent for everyone. If you rent a home in King Shellfish's kingdom, the rent will be set by the great shellfish leader himself. Hints King Shellfish loves when people rent from him. Imagine him rolling in all of the rent money (shellfish) he collected from all the people who rent from him. Hear his shell clattering as he frolics on all the dead shells from the shellfish.
readingMnemonic: If you don't have enough shellfish to pay your rent , King Shellfish will punch you in the chin ( ちん ). Hints Feel your entire body shaking, but especially your chin, as you tell him you're two shellfish short on rent this month. The last thing you see is his big fist coming right for your chin.

meaningMnemonic: Writing a poem about winter is the only way to get respect from other poets. Hints Even better, write a poem about winter IN winter. Then they'll really respect you.
readingMnemonic: Once you have their respect you get ca ke ( けい )! Hints The cake has the word RESPECT in fancy, cursive letters. Imagine eating that cake and taste the respect of your poet peers. Mm mm!

meaningMnemonic: The horns of the creatures who drink alcohol have a measurement so large that they are revered the world over. The horns are revered both for their size and potency. The horns can be used in medicine, so they are very valuable, those alcoholic monster horns. Hints Look at one of these revered horns. Pick it up and feel its weight. It measures very large. Your arms are getting tired from the weight.
readingMnemonic: The reason you are interested in these revered horns so much is that your son ( そん ) is sick and you need one of these revered horns to make a medicine for your son. Only with the revered power of the horns will you be able to save your son’s life. Hints Good thing you already have one of these revered horns. Now imagine yourself grinding it up into a powder to mix into a potion for your son to drink. Hear the horn grinding away as you physically break the horn up into millions of tiny pieces.

meaningMnemonic: If you receive something edible, arrange it in a circle and boil it. That way, it’ll ripen more quickly. Hints Picture yourself receiving something, arranging it in a circle in the pan, and leaving it to boil. See how quickly that stuff ripens? Now it’s all ripe and yummy.
readingMnemonic: Once everything you received has ripen ed, you kick back near your juke box ( じゅく ) and eat it. The jukebox sets the mood, making the ripened treat feels twice as sweet. Hints Imagine the jukebox playing music to accompany your ripened treat. Ahh, jukebox music and ripened goodies. Can life get any sweeter?

meaningMnemonic: Next to your mouth there are fins which react to alcohol . If you exceed a certain alcohol measurement , they start flapping about, which makes you spread rumors and gossip uncontrollably. Hints Just imagine these fins forcing your mouth to move with all their flapping. This is what happens when you have too much alcohol, you can't control yourself.
readingMnemonic: The flapping fins are making you slur your words, but that doesn't stop you from spreading rumors and gossip : " Ooo whassa t ( うわさ ) I hear about so and so having an affair?!" Hints Just imagine trying to talk eloquently and clearly when you have fins flapping around your mouth. And if you've had a few drinks on top of that, it stands to reason that you'd start slurring your words.

meaningMnemonic: If you grind a stone down to more than just a few pieces, it will become sand . Stones that get broken up enough will become sand, and you pick up a few grains in your hand. Hints Feel these few grains of sand between your fingertips. Imagine the stones that they originally came from. Nature is crazy.
readingMnemonic: After breaking up your stone into sand , you fetch your special sand sa w ( さ ). A few bits are still too chunky, so you'll have to use a sand saw now. Hints You may wonder what a sand saw is. Well, it's a saw for cutting sand into even finer little pieces. How does it work? It's a mystery!

meaningMnemonic: You line up stalks of bamboo with an equal interval between each one. This pattern creates a sense of simplicity . Hints Bamboo, interval, bamboo, interval, bamboo… Almost like a binary rhythm: 1, 0, 1, 0, 1. Now that's simplicity. It doesn't get simpler than that!
readingMnemonic: That kind of simplicity is what Genghis Khan ( かん ) always demanded. Everything he decided was based on simplicity. Hints Simplicity is how he took over the world. Attack or don't attack? Boom, simple. If he hadn't stuck to simplicity, he wouldn't have been able to do what he did. Complex thoughts just get in the way of expansionist ambitions, you know?

meaningMnemonic: A leader in boot s has a slight edge over one without boots. It's not much, but even a little advantage is better than nothing. Hints Imagine your leader wearing knee-high leather boots. Wouldn't you feel a little more confident in a leader with boots like that?
readingMnemonic: Getting that slight edge over other leaders allows your leader to become the kin g ( きん ). Hints Your leader must've already been on the verge of becoming king if the slight advantage from those boots was enough to tip the scales.

meaningMnemonic: If you take the flowers off some coral and boil them, steam comes out. Hints Steam comes out of the coral flowers because they hold a lot of water. They're flowers, but they're coral flowers, so they came from the ocean. Of course there's water in them, and if you boil that water steam will come out.
readingMnemonic: As you watch the steam coming off the coral flowers, someone appears behind you. It’s Joe ( じょう ), the big farmhand. "Are you steaming coral?" he asks. "Smelled it a mile away. I love steaming me some coral.” Hints It's weird that Joe is so sensitive to the smell of steaming coral. He's lived as a farmhand nowhere near the sea all his life... at least that's what he told you. And now he's in your house breathing in the steam really deeply with his nose practically in the pot.

meaningMnemonic: The storehouse radical and the storehouse kanji meanings are the same. If you know the radical, you know the kanji! Hints Your brain is like a storehouse, you know? Hopefully that's where you kept your storehouse knowledge.
readingMnemonic: You have a storehouse . Inside is where you keep all your zo mbies ( ぞう ). Hints Be really proud of your storehouse. You've collected a lot of zombies and put them in there, where they'll keep fresh a long time!

meaningMnemonic: Drag some rice over to a canopy where you use a stick to mash it up inside Wolverine 's mouth . Scrape out the mashed-up rice paste, and voila — you've made sugar ! Hints Taste that sweet, sweet sugar. Not many people know, but this is how it's made. The canopy is needed for temperature control, and Wolverine… well, he's got special enzymes in his mouth or something.
readingMnemonic: You learned how to make this kind of sugar in とう きょう . You found a special とうきょう sugar sensei and they introduced you to all the secret methods you know now. Hints Whenever you taste this sugar, you picture とうきょう . It's the place where you fell in love with these strange sugar-making techniques, after all.

meaningMnemonic: The thread you have inside is your whole supply . When you're outside sewing and you run out, you just go inside, look through your supply, and pick a new one. Hints Go inside your house or shed, it doesn't matter where, and look happily at your thread supply. You have thread in all sizes, shapes, and especially colors.
readingMnemonic: You have this supply because No stradamus ( のう ) had a prediction, saying you would. And that if you didn't keep a good supply of thread inside, you'd run out. Hints Nostradamus says you should have a large supply of everything you use regularly. Thread, water, canned foods. You can't see the future, but he can, and if he's telling you to stock up on your inside supplies I think you should listen.

meaningMnemonic: They say someone with various talents is important. Various talents can include speaking various languages so if you are someone who knows various languages you can say things that various peoples will comprehend. Hints You are someone who can say things in various languages. Speak some of these various languages now. You are someone who is good at saying things. Nice job.
readingMnemonic: You’re so good at speaking various languages that you decide to put on a sho w ( しょ ). At the show, you say a lot of things in various languages and everyone is impressed. Hints Imagine yourself at this show. The spotlight is on and all eyes are watching. You feel kind of nervous, but you speak the various languages with ease.

meaningMnemonic: The hole leading to the private heart of your house is the window . Or maybe it's just the window to your soul, and not your house. Like the poetry people say. Hints Imagine someone looking into a hole that shows your private heart. That's a window. A window you probably should have kept closed. Now everyone is looking in.
readingMnemonic: You realize that a ton of people are looking into your window and seeing all your private things. This makes you mad ( まど )! What right do they have to know your private thoughts and desires?! Hints Look out your window back at the faces. Try to express how mad you are at them with your face through the glass. Make as many mad faces that you can think of.

Or, when it comes to transmitting all the things a leader proclaims, you can also call it propaganda .

meaningMnemonic: 散る is "to be scattered." 散らかす on the other hand is when you're doing the scattering. So it means to scatter or to make a mess . You often hear it when someone talks about making a room messy or leaving things all over the place. You can remember it easily because after a ruckus ( らかす ), people often leave a mess behind.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how 離れる means "to separate," where something separates or moves away from something else? Well, 離す is the transitive version, so it takes a direct object and means to separate something . You can remember this because if you try to separate two people who don't want to be separated, they might sue ( す ) you in response! 離す is used when you detach or put space between people or objects. This could be literal, like when you 離す your bed from the wall, or more figurative, like when you carelessly 離す your eyes from something important. It can also mean to let go of something, because you're "separating" your hand from it. This use is very similar to 放す , but it doesn't have that nuance of setting something free — it's just the neutral act of letting go of something.
readingMnemonic: The reading comes from 離れる .

meaningMnemonic: You have the kanji for wipe , and this is the verb version of that, which makes this to wipe or to mop up . You've already learned 拭く , which is a general word for the act of wiping, whether you're wiping a table or wiping your forehead. 拭う , on the other hand, is more commonly used in writing to describe the act of wiping away and removing something specific like sweat, tears, filth, or even doubts.
readingMnemonic: This is a verb, so it uses the kun'yomi. However, to differentiate this verb from 拭く , it uses a different reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember this: What are you trying to wipe ? Some nu de goo ( ぬぐ )! You spilled nude goo all over your floor, and now you have to mop it all up… pesky nude goo.
